correctness.rationale: Every stable active PAV pooling regime is a consecutive-block weighted-average linear map and each partition can occur on an open cone. Piecewise linear segment subdivision reduces the global two-input Lipschitz bound to maximum of these matrix seminorms; the coarea identity for unweighted complete-pair Gini reduces each matrix norm to binary cuts. Every extremizing cut is locally attainable. Since block indicators lie in [0,1]^n, G≤floor(n²/4), while input cut costs at least n−1, yielding universal C_n; dominant mass in a near-balanced pooled block gives sharp supremum but not attainment for fixed positive masses. A separate singleton/two-element block calculation gives exact n=4 expression, adjacent mass-ratio ≤3 nonexpansivity. Independently enumerated partition-cut values with exact fractions for n=3,4,5, obtaining n=4 μ=(4,1,1,1) value 16/15.
